indicators.note: arrangements of a word's letters set them out in a new order, so the word beside it is reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up other ways to organise a pause or holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: the pause in a cricket match or working day for a cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause for a cup and biscuits is a short rest from work or play.

explanation.surface: A description of something level and with right angles.
explanation.definitionFit: Level ground is smooth and flat; to be square is to be quits, owing nothing.

parts.note: reads like a banner of many colours, but flag is also a name for a garden plant of the lily-like kind named after the rainbow goddess

explanation.surface: A banner in many colours flutters overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is an old name for this plant, whose flowers come in many colours, like the rainbow it is named for.

clue.text: They supply brewed drinks on tap

definitions.text: They supply brewed drinks on tap

parts.words: They supply brewed drinks on tap
parts.note: on tap suggests beer from a pub barrel, but these large vessels with taps dispense hot drinks from leaves

explanation.surface: A pub's beer pumps serve home-brewed ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Big metal boilers with a tap at the bottom serve hot infused drinks at canteens and fêtes.

explanation.surface: An evening of dancing followed by a dip in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Scottish country dance; and when your head swims, it spins and you stagger.

parts.note: read as a casual phrase about making do, it literally means that with this quality a person is able to do things

explanation.surface: A shrug: this will do, one can manage.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacity or skill is what makes a person able to accomplish something.

parts.note: sounds like starting a machine, but going means leaving, so it is a present for someone departing

explanation.surface: An instruction to start an engine or project.
explanation.definitionFit: A present handed to a colleague who is leaving a job is received as they depart.

parts.note: sounds like pity for a small animal, but alludes to the saying poor as one living in a place of worship

explanation.surface: Sympathy for some small, pitiable animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The British saying 'as poor as a church mouse' means having nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially the poorest of rodents, since a place of worship holds no food to steal.

explanation.surface: Advice to a sprinter to keep to a direct course.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprint is a quick short run; a short horizontal stroke in punctuation is also so called.

indicators.note: action applied to the word beside it sets its letters to work in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Hasty measures are taken on behalf of a traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling worker who moves from place to place is described by this word for wandering.

explanation.surface: A couple shift position during a cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift slightly or rouse; and a turn of a spoon round a cup mixes its contents.

parts.note: looks like a diet, but habits are garments, here formal clothes worn for an evening meal

explanation.surface: A remark about someone's diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Black-tie outfits are the formal clothing worn to an evening meal.

parts.note: late suggests tardy arrivals, but here it means deceased, entering heaven through its legendary entrance

explanation.surface: A side door kept for people who turn up late.
explanation.definitionFit: The gates of heaven, made of pearl in Revelation, admit the dead.

clue.text: I'd learn about part of the British Isles

indicators.note: about here means in a turned-around state, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student promises to study a region of the British Isles.
explanation.definitionFit: The island west of Great Britain is one of the two main islands of the British Isles.

clue.text: Boy of six embraced by his father

indicators.note: being embraced means being held inside another's arms, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an informal word for one's father is dad
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A six-year-old boy is hugged by his dad.
explanation.definitionFit: A common given name for a male, like the young giant-slaying shepherd of the Bible.

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a faithful reservoir wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow, as a barrier does a river; and steadfastly faithful.

clue.text: Like a judge with robes in disarray

indicators.note: something in disarray is in a muddle, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

explanation.surface: A judge sits in court with his gown dishevelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like a judge' refers to the saying 'sober as a judge'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying calls a judge the model of a clear head, free from drink.

clue.text: A green and mountainous part of France

explanation.surface: A description of an Alpine French region's lush hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A crinkly-leaved cabbage variety is a green vegetable; the Alpine region on the Italian border bears the same name.

clue.text: He ruled in one Roman era

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A statement about a ruler in a period of Roman history.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor who reigned in Rome from AD 54 to 68 was a ruler.

clue.text: Iago upset by cost of changing money

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: the villain of Othello

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's villain is irritated by exchange fees.
explanation.definitionFit: A premium or charge paid for exchanging one currency for another.

indicators.note: to here means added into, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to help out is to aid
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was told to come and assist.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointed or steered towards a target, as a remark or weapon is.

parts.note: suggests a heap of goods from a factory, but the workers are insects famed for hard work

explanation.surface: Hard-working labourers produce a stack of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound of earth heaped up by colonies of insects known for their diligence.

clue.text: Very keen supporter voted out on two points

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is east, a compass point, taken twice

explanation.surface: A loyal fan is voted off by a narrow margin.
explanation.definitionFit: An enthusiast or ardent follower is wholly dedicated to a cause.

clue.text: He's right to take Monday off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of the day are scrambled

explanation.surface: A worker is entitled to a day off at the start of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: A male given name, so 'he' stands for a man so called.

explanation.surface: Someone tidies their shoes twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub is to brush someone aside; to buff is to polish, so doing it again is a second shine.

parts.note: something erect is standing up
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something stands tall like a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisonous Javanese tree of legend, whose sap was used on arrows.

indicators.note: out here means outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A firm finds a way to escape paying tax.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a levy or payment, as in the phrase scot-free.

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look

explanation.surface: Advice to watch when raising one's eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a rule or a festival is to observe or honour it.

parts.note: sounds like a pause for rest, but read literally it is the organ where breathing happens

explanation.surface: A pause or respite to recover.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the two chest organs that fill with air when we inhale.

clue.text: Coshed quite badly in the dance hall

indicators.note: badly means done wrongly, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A brawl in a dance hall leaves someone clubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub where people dance to recorded music is a modern dance venue.

explanation.surface: Rules are placed on knockout football games.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football a cup tie is a knockout match in a cup competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonds or constraints restrict; knockout fixtures in a cup competition are also so called.

parts.note: suggests ships of a shipping line, but these grip washing on a clothes line

explanation.surface: A query about fast sailing ships of a shipping company.
explanation.definitionFit: Small wooden or plastic grips hold laundry on a washing line.
